subject: math.GN
name: Hilbert–Smith conjecture
statement: Must every locally compact group admitting a faithful continuous action on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold be a Lie group?
importance: It asks whether manifold topology excludes genuinely non-Lie continuous symmetries.
status_note: The conjecture is proved in dimensions at most three and for several more regular action classes; arbitrary continuous actions in higher dimensions remain open.

subject: math.GN
name: Bing–Borsuk conjecture
statement: Is every finite-dimensional locally compact homogeneous separable metric absolute neighborhood retract a topological manifold?
importance: It seeks a characterization of manifolds using local homotopy regularity and the ability to move any point to any other.
status_note: The low-dimensional cases are known; homogeneity without the ANR hypothesis does not suffice.

subject: math.GN
name: Busemann manifold conjecture
statement: Is every finite-dimensional Busemann G-space a topological manifold? Here a G-space is a proper geodesic metric space with local geodesic extension and unique local continuation in Busemann’s sense.
importance: It asks whether natural intrinsic geodesic axioms already force manifold topology.
status_note: The conjecture is known in dimensions at most four. A 2026 result establishes the disjoint disks property in dimensions at least five, leaving the resolution obstruction.

references.title: The disjoint disks property for Busemann G-spaces

subject: math.GN
name: Michael-space problem in ZFC
statement: Can ZFC alone establish the existence of a regular Lindelöf space X for which X × (R minus Q), with the usual topology on the irrationals, is not Lindelöf?
importance: It is a central test of when the Lindelöf property survives products.
status_note: Examples exist under additional set-theoretic assumptions; existence without such assumptions remains open.

subject: math.GN
name: Efimov-space existence problem in ZFC
statement: Can ZFC alone establish the existence of an infinite compact Hausdorff space containing neither a nontrivial convergent sequence nor a subspace homeomorphic to the Stone–Čech compactification βN?
importance: It asks whether infinite compact spaces must exhibit one of two fundamental types of infinite behavior.
status_note: Efimov spaces are known under additional set-theoretic assumptions; the unresolved question is their existence from ZFC alone.

subject: math.GN
name: D-space problem for regular Lindelöf spaces
statement: Is every regular Hausdorff Lindelöf space a D-space: for each assignment of an open neighborhood U_x to every point x, is there a closed discrete set D such that the sets U_x for x in D cover the space?
importance: It asks whether countable-cover compactness forces discrete selection of prescribed neighborhoods.
status_note: Known nonregular counterexamples do not settle the regular Hausdorff case; Menger spaces and many classical classes are D-spaces.

subject: math.GN
name: D-space problem for paracompact spaces
statement: Is every paracompact Hausdorff space a D-space, meaning every open-neighborhood assignment has a covering subfamily indexed by a closed discrete set?
importance: It asks whether locally finite refinements always yield a much more constrained discrete neighborhood selection.
status_note: Paracompactness is not known to imply the D-property in full generality; metric spaces and many special paracompact classes satisfy it.

subject: math.GN
name: Plane fixed-point problem
statement: Does every nonseparating plane continuum have the fixed-point property for all its continuous self-maps, where a continuum is a nonempty compact connected subset of R^2 and nonseparating means its complement is connected?
importance: It extends the Brouwer fixed-point theorem to arbitrary connected planar sets without holes.
status_note: The problem is open without local connectedness or other extra hypotheses; results about extensions to plane homeomorphisms are weaker statements.

references.title: Fixed-point property and the plane fixed-point problem

subject: math.GN
name: Small-diagonal compact-space problem
statement: Must a compact Hausdorff space X be metrizable if, for every uncountable set A contained in X × X minus the diagonal, some open neighborhood U of the diagonal has A minus U uncountable?
importance: It asks whether a weak diagonal-separation condition characterizes metric compact spaces.
status_note: The displayed condition is the small-diagonal property; it is weaker than having a G_δ diagonal, whose compact metrization theorem is known.

references.title: Elementary chains and compact spaces with a small diagonal

subject: math.GN
name: Homogeneous tree-like continuum problem
statement: Is every nondegenerate homogeneous tree-like metric continuum homeomorphic to the pseudo-arc, where tree-like means admitting continuous surjections to finite trees whose fibers all have diameter less than any prescribed positive ε?
importance: It seeks a classification of homogeneous continua with the shape of a point.
status_note: The homogeneous chainable case is known; the broader tree-like case remains open.
